name: Solana public mainnet-beta JSON-RPC (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com)
operator: Solana Foundation (public cluster endpoint published in the Solana documentation; answers name the serving RPC node in x-rpc-node)
tier_rationale: Established foundation that stewards the Solana protocol and publishes the public cluster endpoints, their rate limits and the 'not intended for production' caveat in its documentation (A8 trusted: established organisation with published terms). Binding council decision P215 FC3: registry provider solana_foundation, tier trusted.

reliability.justification: Ledger state served by a public node, best effort with no SLA. From a datacenter egress on 2026-11-26 the endpoint answered a valid-looking 0 lamports / [] for an account that certainly exists (Circle's USDC mint), while it answered the System Program correctly in the same minute: empty answers are not proof of absence.

rpc.title: Solana mainnet-beta public JSON-RPC: getBalance and getSignaturesForAddress (limit <= 25) only

terms.quote: Registry provider solana_foundation: tier trusted, terms open (public RPC, best effort, no SLA).

rpc.notes: Quote: binding council text (P215 FC3); the research record (C0502) gives 'Solana Foundation public RPC (best-effort, no SLA)' and 'Public RPC: ~100 req/10 s per IP, 40 req/10 s per method (Solana docs); not for heavy use'. The evidence page answered a Vercel Security Checkpoint (HTTP 429) from the datacenter egress on 2026-11-26: doctor --licences --refresh must report it BLOCKED challenge, never 'terms changed'. The quota block uses the stricter OBSERVED figure (published=false): live x-ratelimit headers gave getSignaturesForAddress a method limit of 10 (getBalance 150, rps 250, conn/connrate 40); 1 request/s x 0.8 = 8 requests per 10 s for the whole provider. The day budget of 1000 is a team policy (the endpoint is 'not intended for production'), not a published limit. JSON-RPC errors arrive inside HTTP 200 (e.g. -32602 'Invalid param'): the markers cover rate limit (429), egress block (403) and disabled calls (410); other JSON-RPC errors are classified by the module as ERROR (could not verify).

notes: Owned by batch p3-G09-2 (P215 solana_rpc). Only the read-only methods getBalance and getSignaturesForAddress are ever sent (never sendTransaction, requestAirdrop, getTransaction or getTokenAccountsByOwner). A bare base58 string is never sent: the module runs only on explicitly typed Solana inputs (FC2).
